questions.unit: Features and Presentation of Ovarian Cancers
questions.q: Why is screening for ovarian cancer printed as not done?
opts: Because it affects only old women

questions.unit: Features and Presentation of Ovarian Cancers
questions.q: The printed presentation symptoms of ovarian cancer are:
opts: Vague symptoms such as nausea/vomiting and loss of appetite
questions.exp: 'Vague symptoms (Nausea/Vomiting, Loss of appetite)'.

questions.exp: 'Adnexal masses (IOC : TVS)'.

questions.unit: Features and Presentation of Ovarian Cancers
questions.q: True/False: Ovarian cancer typically presents with specific early symptoms according to the printed page.
opts: False - it presents with acute abdomen always
questions.exp: The printed presentation is vague symptoms, which is why prognosis is poor.

questions.q: Benign adnexal masses are most common in which group?
questions.exp: The prevalence row prints m/c in reproductive age group for benign.

questions.q: Malignant adnexal masses are printed at which ages?
opts: Extremes of age: pre-pubertal and menopausal
questions.exp: The malignant prevalence cell prints extremes of age.

questions.q: Pain in a benign adnexal mass is printed as positive due to:
questions.exp: The benign pain cell prints plus with '(d/t inflammation)'.

questions.q: The history printed for a malignant adnexal mass is:

questions.exp: The malignant history cell prints exactly that.

questions.q: Match each attribute with its benign and malignant values - 1) Occurrence 2) Consistency 3) Tenderness ... A) Benign unilateral, malignant bilateral B) Benign cystic, malignant solid C) Benign positive, malignant negative ... choose:

questions.q: Which ultrasound features are printed for a benign adnexal mass?
opts: Bilateral, echogenic, multilocular with solid component
Unilateral, anechoic, unilocular with no solid component
Bilateral, anechoic, unilocular with thick septa
questions.exp: The benign ultrasound cell lists U/L, anechoic, unilocular and solid component minus.

questions.q: The size threshold printed in the malignant ultrasound column is:
questions.exp: The malignant cell opens with 'B/L, > 10 cm size'.

questions.q: Thick septa with papillary outgrowths in the malignant column are also called:
questions.exp: The bracket prints '(Excrescences)' after papillary outgrowths.

questions.q: Which additional malignant ultrasound signs are printed beyond septa and vascularity?

questions.exp: The benign column prints solid component minus; solid components belong to malignancy.

questions.exp: Anechoic unilocular is benign; the rest are malignant column entries.

Thin septa, mural oedema, papillary projections and cystic components

Thick septa, mural nodularity, acoustic shadowing and solid components

questions.unit: Ultrasound Features Suggestive of Ovarian Malignancy

questions.exp: The image text overlays read SOLID COMPONENT and SEPTAE.

questions.exp: '> 7 cm -> Surgery (High chances surgery of torsion or rupture)'.

questions.exp: The bracket prints high chances surgery of torsion or rupture.

questions.exp: 'CA 125 >= 35 IU -> Surgery after further investigations'.

questions.exp: The pre-pubertal arm prints 'If any raised : AFP, HCG, LDH'.
